title: Key Project Constraints
subtitle: Six tensions every project manager must balance
items: [{"heading":"Scope vs Speed","body":"More features mean longer timelines. Agreeing upfront which scope items are negotiable prevents teams being locked into unrealistic schedules."},{"heading":"Quality vs Cost","body":"Cutting QA saves money short-term but compounds rework costs later. Quality investment pays back at 3-5x in reduced defects post-launch."},{"heading":"Innovation vs Risk","body":"Novel approaches carry higher uncertainty. A proven pattern with known constraints often outperforms a speculative solution that introduces unknown failure modes."},{"heading":"Autonomy vs Alignment","body":"Full team autonomy can produce divergent solutions. Regular alignment checkpoints preserve creative freedom while keeping outputs coherent."},{"heading":"Speed vs Stability","body":"Moving fast without documentation creates brittle systems. The sustainable delivery rate is the one the team can maintain for the whole project."},{"heading":"Detail vs Clarity","body":"Overly detailed specifications overwhelm stakeholders. Executive communication requires ruthless prioritisation of what matters most."}]
